24.text: is quite unfit for the saddle, and is not so strong in the harness, especially

26.text: since it fattens quickly, and does not lose its fat as easily. In good pasture

27.text: the Chukchee reindeer accumulates so much fat that its whole body is covered

28.text: with it. On the hind part, near the tail, the fat is about two inches thick.

29.text: At present a brisk trade in reindeer is carried on between the Lamut,

30.text: and the Chukchee. The Lamut reindeer commands about twice the price of

31.text: the Chukchee reindeer. Usually a Lamut fawn is exchanged for a grown

32.text: Chukchee reindeer. A broken Lamut reindeer is worth three Chukchee rein-

33.text: deer; and the Lamut and the Tungus often break all the young bucks in

34.text: their herds in order to barter them away to the Chukchee. Therefore the

35.text: larger portion of Chukchee harness-reindeer are at the present time of the

36.text: Lamut race. The Lamut, on the other hand, have stopped slaughtering their

37.text: own reindeer, because they can always get Chukchee reindeer, which are

38.text: cheaper, and better fitted for the purpose.
